summary: Failure events are swallowed — WebSocket close codes (1002/1006) and missing post-call webhooks are not mapped or surfaced to the operator/dashboard
root_cause: By design today the system favours never auto-disabling the webhook (endpoint always returns 200) and routes failures to encrypted DLQs, but there is no mapping of ElevenLabs/Twilio close codes or DLQ/missing-webhook events to a user-visible status or alert. Result: a dropped or abnormally-closed call (e.g. BUG-005 1006, BUG-001/002 1002) is invisible unless someone reads container logs on the VM.
evidence: Raised by tester to Rajveer via WhatsApp 2026-06-11 08:45: 'We need to map the error code and when/If received it should be handled and communicated on the other entity.' Currently unacknowledged. Concrete instances already observed: 1002 (BUG-001/002), 1006 (BUG-005), webhook-not-received (noted by Rajveer on the 5s call, 2026-06-09). Relevant code: server/routes/webhooks.py (always-200 + DLQ), server/websocket.py (close handling), utils/alerts.py (unused alert path).
suggested_fix: Define an error-code -> handling/notification map: classify EL/Twilio close codes (1002 config, 1006 abnormal, 1000 normal) and missing-webhook/DLQ events, then surface terminal failures to the dashboard and/or an ops alert (utils/alerts.py) instead of only logging. Makes call failures observable to the operator in real time rather than via VM log archaeology.
